_doc: USER-EDITABLE seed source registry for Harness Radar — the coding-HARNESS (AI coding agent / scaffold) sibling of Model Radar's sources.json. Edit this file directly to add, remove, or retag sources; it is data, not code. Each source's stance_hint is a DEFAULT only: extraction may override the stance per evidence item. stance_hint must be one of the dossier-schema.json stance enum values: maker_claim | independent_eval | practitioner_take. TO ADD A SOURCE: append an object to 'sources' with a unique id (lowercase-hyphenated), kind ('maker_page' for a harness maker's blog/releases/docs page, 'youtube_channel' for a channel), name, stance_hint, and a note. For maker_page also set url and maker; for a harness maker also set harness_slugs (which harness dossiers this source primarily feeds). For youtube_channel also set channel_id and rss_url in the keyless form https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=<CHANNEL_ID> (same convention as cse/skills/scout/youtube_rss.py — no API key required). LEADERBOARDS SECTION: the top-level 'leaderboards' array registers NUMERIC score sources — living leaderboard/eval websites harvested for score snapshots conforming to score-schema.json. THE HARNESS TWIST: harness leaderboard rows are almost always harness+model COMBOS (a 'system'/'scaffold' running an underlying model), so parsing must map the system/scaffold to harness_slug and the underlying model to model_slug, and record the scaffold configuration in 'config'. Each leaderboard entry is an INDEPENDENT best-effort rung: enabled entries are all attempted per run, a failed fetch/parse NEVER aborts the run, and every attempt (fetched | parsed | failed + snapshot_count) is recorded in the run's source_health_report. Per-entry fields: id (slug, becomes score_snapshot.source_slug), kind 'leaderboard', name, url, stance_hint (always 'independent_eval'), enabled (flip to false to skip a rung without deleting it), benchmark_slugs, metrics, parse_hints, note.

sources.name: All Hands AI Blog
sources.note: Maker of OpenHands (ex-OpenDevin) — release posts, CodeAct agent updates, and headline SWE-bench claims for the leading open-source harness.

sources.name: Aider Blog
sources.note: Maker of Aider (terminal pair-programmer) — also runs the Aider polyglot leaderboard; posts on repo-map, edit formats, and model rankings under a fixed harness.

sources.name: Pi (earendil-works) Releases
sources.note: Maker of Pi — the minimal 4-tool (read/write/edit/bash) BYOK terminal harness that self-extends via extensions/skills/packages. Publishes no benchmarks by design (favors real-session data); harvest release notes for capability/architecture claims.

sources.name: Anthropic Engineering / News (Claude Code)
sources.note: Anthropic's engineering + news posts covering Claude Code — the repo-aware terminal/IDE agent; harness-vs-harness eval posts (e.g. same Opus swinging 77%->93% across harnesses) live here.

sources.name: OpenAI Codex Releases
sources.note: OpenAI Codex — Apache-2.0 Rust CLI (open) plus the closed cloud SWE agent. Release notes carry GPT-5-Codex SWE-bench + Terminal-Bench claims and CLI capability changes.

sources.name: Cursor Blog
sources.note: Cursor (VS Code-fork IDE agent + in-house Composer model) release + benchmark posts (Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Multilingual).

sources.name: Goose (Block) Blog
sources.note: Goose — MCP-native desktop/CLI agent that drives any LLM to real actions; ships its own `goose bench`. Strong feed for the tool_integration axis.

sources.name: Theo (t3dotgg)
sources.note: Working engineer's hands-on takes on coding agents and dev tooling — fast, opinionated, builder-perspective reactions to Cursor / Cline / Claude Code / Codex and OSS harnesses.

sources.name: AI Explained
sources.note: Careful independent analysis of agent + benchmark claims — scrutinizes SWE-bench validity, contamination, and the harness-vs-model confound.

sources.name: Matthew Berman
sources.note: High-volume hands-on agent testing and AI-news coverage — informal test suites and early practitioner impressions of new coding agents/harnesses.

leaderboards.name: SWE-bench Leaderboard
leaderboards.parse_hints: Leaderboard tables per split (Verified / full / Lite / bash-only). Map the Verified tab to benchmark_slug 'swe-bench-verified' and the full split to 'swe-bench'. CRITICAL FOR HARNESS RADAR: each row is a SYSTEM (scaffold/harness) running an underlying MODEL — map the system/scaffold name to harness_slug (e.g. 'OpenHands + CodeAct' -> harness_slug 'openhands', config 'CodeAct v3'), and the underlying model to model_slug (e.g. 'Opus 4.6' -> 'claude-opus-4-6'). Record the scaffold in 'config'. The bash-only track (mini-SWE-agent) maps to harness_slug 'swe-agent', config 'bash-only'. Scope to the top ~15 systems + any existing-dossier harnesses. If client-rendered, use the r.jina.ai fallback.
leaderboards.note: The headline real-world coding benchmark — resolved-rate on real GitHub issues; PRIMARY numeric feed for the 'agentic_capability' axis. Every entry is a harness+model combo, so this is the core Harness Radar leaderboard. Heavily contaminated + scaffold-sensitive: always capture the underlying model + config.

leaderboards.name: Terminal-Bench
leaderboards.parse_hints: Laude Institute + Stanford leaderboard — agents autonomously plan/execute/recover through a shell (compile, configure, admin, data tasks). Rows are agent (harness) + model combos: map the agent to harness_slug, the model to model_slug. Terminal-Bench 2.0 (89 tasks) is the current split — record 'terminal-bench-2' in config or notes when the page distinguishes versions. Academic, no commercial stake -> a high-credibility independent feed for 'agentic_capability'. Use the r.jina.ai fallback if client-rendered.
leaderboards.note: High-credibility academic benchmark for autonomous multi-step shell task completion — a strong independent 'agentic_capability' feed that all three of Anthropic / OpenAI / Cursor report. Small N -> higher variance.

leaderboards.name: Aider Polyglot Leaderboard
leaderboards.parse_hints: Static docs page with an HTML table: model name, 'Percent completed correctly' (metric 'accuracy'), edit format, and total cost. NOTE: this leaderboard ranks MODELS under the FIXED Aider harness, so EVERY row's harness_slug is 'aider' and model_slug is the listed model; record the edit format (e.g. 'diff', 'whole') in 'config' and the cost column as a separate usd_per_task snapshot (feeds the emergent 'token_efficiency' axis). Usually parseable from a plain fetch without the r.jina.ai fallback.
leaderboards.note: Practical multi-language code-editing benchmark from the Aider project — a fixed-harness signal that isolates MODEL editing skill while pinning harness_slug='aider'. Its cost column is the best public per-task $ data for token-efficiency context.

leaderboards.name: SWE-bench Pro (Scale SEAL)
leaderboards.parse_hints: Scale AI / SEAL harder, longer-horizon, partly-private, contamination-resistant SWE task set (731 tasks). Rows are harness+model combos: map to harness_slug + model_slug, record config. Independent curation -> more credible than vendor Verified numbers, but still shows 5-10pt harness swings (e.g. Opus 4.5 45.9% SEAL vs 55.4% via Claude Code). Use the r.jina.ai fallback if client-rendered; if the page is unavailable, record 'failed' and continue.
leaderboards.note: Contamination-resistant harder SWE benchmark OpenAI now recommends over Verified — a higher-credibility 'agentic_capability' feed. Still scaffold-sensitive; always capture harness + config.

leaderboards.name: Konwinski Prize (K Prize)
leaderboards.parse_hints: Contamination-free SWE-bench variant: the test set is built ONLY from GitHub issues filed AFTER the submission deadline, so train-set leakage is impossible. Numbers are brutally low (round-1 top ~7.5%) and surface via Kaggle + announcement pages, not a live scrapable board — DISABLED by default; enable and parse best-effort from announcement/Kaggle pages, setting source_url to the actual report. The gold standard for anti-contamination rigor and the honest floor for real-world generalization.
leaderboards.note: The anti-contamination gold standard ($1M Kaggle prize). Low scores expose the real-world gap that heavily-contaminated Verified numbers hide. Off by default (no living board); harvest via announcements.
